BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## Threshold point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"
The note says the [STANDARD] clauses were "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the disclosure and limitation package is "already accepted". That is the Seller's assertion, not our position. Nothing in our file shows Wattlebridge has cleared any of it, and several [STANDARD] items conflict directly with the playbook. I have reviewed every item and recommend we reply in writing that no position is agreed until the full SPA is settled. The cover letter's "negotiated positions" and "agreed price mechanics" wording should be rejected the same way.

## 1. Liability regime: material departures

| Item | Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6m | The Seller has opened at our *fallback*. That fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority naming the draft, and none exists. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m and do not signal flexibility. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our figure. Small claims would be systematically excluded. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | 5x our figure, and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. Together with the de minimis, the real recoverable value of warranties shrinks substantially. |
| Claims period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is also a fallback needing Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Hold 24 months. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Sweeps in everything | Separate regimes | This is a hidden override. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud into the general limits. Reject it. Each category should state its own limits. |

## 2. Fundamental/Title and fraud
- **Title and capacity "same caps and time limits… for administrative simplicity":** reject. Our position is a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. A 20%/18-month limit on title to 100% of the shares would leave us badly exposed on the core asset.
- **Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature":** these limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions have no fraud carve-out. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable on our side, so the drafting must say so expressly.

## 3. Disclosure and knowledge
- **Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2:** the Seller discloses the entire data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records against the warranties. That is exactly the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure we reject. Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Letter 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable only if it does not undercut the warranties or indemnities.
- **Clause 8.3 (buyer knowledge):** this is a blanket exclusion covering knowledge of the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. It is constructive knowledge plus the data-room disclosure by another route, and it would gut the warranties because we are the party doing the diligence. Delete it. If a qualifier is conceded anywhere, it should be on named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and never for title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Letter 11 ("the Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts…"):** this is an attempt to shift risk to us. We should not accept it as an acknowledgement.

## 4. Conditions and closing deliverables

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, about 30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller's own letter (para 2) admits there is no final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are met. Yet the draft proposes reasonable endeavours and treats consent as "satisfied on delivery". That is the position our playbook rejects. A consent can arrive with unmet conditions, and endeavours alone are insufficient for a customer of this size. Require an effective consent and evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion, as a condition we control.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m).** The facility is not repaid and no discharge is provided (letter para 3). A release "following Completion" would leave us owning a company still under the bank's security. Require a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release is only possible with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval, which we do not have. This is also inherent in the debt-free/cash-free baseline.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000).** The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" but leaves it out of the funds flow. The letter (para 5) concedes the amounts are absent and says nothing about payroll tax, super or other on-costs. The funds flow cannot silently exclude them. Require a specific line item, or Seller funding, covering the AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs. Ask the Seller to confirm which on-costs apply and in what amount. I haven't assumed a figure.

## 5. Specific matters

- **Ironquay IP (clause 11.1):** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and the Seller calls it adequate. Broaden it to cover the wider Ironquay IP exposure, while preserving the SOW3 cure (DD-004 clause 7.3: Project Materials transfer on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee). The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is not independently verified, and the letter itself says so. Do not assume it is owed or paid. Request bank evidence, a payment receipt and a confirmatory assignment.
- **Export/privacy incident (DD-006):** the Seller calls it "not expected to be material", but its own letter (para 6) says the investigation is preliminary and access, scope and notification are unknown. That is not a basis for either side to characterise it. We should not allege a breach or put forward a number. We should require log preservation, a proper investigation, regular updates and cooperation, and ensure the disclosure does not dilute warranty or indemnity protection for it.
- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000):** the Seller says "ordinary-course", but the letter (para 8) does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Request contract terms and commitment status. Do not treat them as Debt or seek a price deduction at this stage. Assess first.
- **Tax and IP:** the Seller says these are "settled under the general regime". They are open. Reject the statement. Keep Tax, IP, Title and payment/covenant categories separate with no override into the general regime. Do not assume unlimited liability or any resolution either way.
- **Title:** DD-012 is the Company's own share register, so it is not independent proof, and the letter (para 10) says as much. Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, for example certified transfer history, ASIC and security searches, confirmation that no charges or options exist over the shares (including under Riverlark security), and Seller authority resolutions.
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** the letter does not say consent is required, but it also does not rule it out. Check the actual clauses against the share-sale structure and add a confirming warranty. This is low priority.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "cleared/[STANDARD]" framing** in writing, and say that nothing is agreed and the whole package is under review.
2. **Counter the limits:** 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24 months. Do not offer 20% or 18 months. Any move needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Delete the "applies to all Claims" language** and put title/fundamental claims on their own regime (100% cap, at least six years, no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar).
4. **Add the fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** to every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause.
5. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure,** and delete clause 8.3. If a knowledge qualifier is conceded, limit it to named persons with reasonable enquiry and exclude title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.
6. **Bluefen:** make effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied a pre-Completion condition.
7. **Riverlark:** require payout, repayment from Completion funds and security releases at Completion. No post-completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval.
8. **Funds flow:** add the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a line item, or make them Seller-funded.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and request independent payment evidence.
10. **Incident:** insist on preservation, investigation and updates, without asserting a breach or a number.
11. **Sandbar:** request details, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
12. **Tax/IP:** keep open and separate, with no general-regime override.
13. **Title:** require independent evidence and do not rely on DD-012 alone.

One further step: someone should check whether any earlier correspondence could be read as accepting the Seller's 20% or 18-month figures. If so, we should expressly reserve our position in the response.
